notes.content: My dad works at a returns desk — and you know how every return counter has a limit? Like, you can only get back what you brought. That's the ceiling at every exchange counter on earth. But Isaiah 61:3 blows that ceiling off. Jehovah doesn't just take your ashes back — he gives you 'a headdress instead of ashes.' Not no ashes. A crown where ashes were. He gives 'the oil of exultation instead of mourning' — not relief from mourning, exultation where mourning lived. Now connect that to Psalm 30:11 — 'You have changed my mourning into dancing.' Same exchange counter. Same upgrade logic. If you walked in here today still wearing something grief handed you — a despondent spirit, a heaviness you can't name — the verse says Jehovah is running a different kind of counter. You don't just leave lighter. You leave called 'big trees of righteousness, the planting of Jehovah.' That's not a return. That's a transformation.
